judged_text: TopicEmbed.import interpolates the embed URL unescaped into the imported_from footer HTML (an <a href='...'> built by string interpolation of the url variable), and the only validation is an anchored ^https?:// regex that permits single quotes, so an embed_url like http://host/?p=1'onmouseover='alert(1) — a valid URI whose host matches embeddable_host — injects an onmouseover attribute into the stored post. An anonymous attacker sends GET /embed/best?embed_url=... with a forged Referer whose host equals embeddable_host, the RetrieveTopic job imports that URL, and the injected event handler is stored in cooked and rendered raw on the topic page and the embed view, firing XSS on mouseover for any viewer — no attacker-controlled content on the embeddable host is required.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer appends HTML containing an `` built via string interpolation (`contents << ... link: "#{url}"`). The only shown validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not escape or reject quotes. The post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, while the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore, if a URL containing a single quote is accepted, it can break out of the `href` attribute and inject additional attributes/JS (stored XSS) into the stored post content and rendered embed/topic views. The diff shows no escaping/sanitization of the footer URL before storing/rendering.
